t:
(a) Grants to States and Territories.—Section 41601(b) of the Violence Against Women Act of 1994 (42 U.S.C. 14043g(b)) is amended—
        (1) in paragraph (1), by striking “other programs” and all that follows and inserting “other nongovernmental or tribal programs and projects to assist individuals who have been 
victimized by sexual assault, without regard to the age of the individual.”; 
        (2) in paragraph (2)—
            (A) in subparagraph (B), by inserting “or tribal programs and activities” after “nongovernmental organizations”; and 
            (B) in subparagraph (C)(v), by striking “linguistically and”; and  
        (3) in paragraph (4)—
            (A) by inserting “(including the District of Columbia and Puerto Rico)” after “The Attorney General shall allocate to each State”; 
            (B) by striking “the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico,” after “Guam”; 
            (C) by striking “0.125 percent” and inserting “0.25 percent”; and 
            (D) by striking “The District of Columbia shall be treated as a territory for purposes of calculating its allocation under the preceding formula.”.   
    (b) Authorization of Appropriations.—Section 41601(f)(1) of the Violence Against Women Act of 1994 (42 U.S.C. 14043g(f)(1)) is amended by striking “$50,000,000 to remain available until expended for each of the fiscal years 2007 through 2011” and inserting “$40,000,000 to remain available until expended for each of fiscal years 2014 through 2018”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that references to States, tribal programs, and nongovernmental organizations signal outside-party involvement. But the section only amends grant purposes, the allocation formula, and the authorization of appropriations for a sexual assault services program. Grant funding and allocation are not consultation, and nothing here provides for comment, a hearing, an advisory body, rulemaking, or a right to sue over a federal decision.
fable.s: The Attorney General shall allocate to each State

qwen_block.w: This section amends the statutory text regarding the allocation of grants to states and territories. It does not establish a process for outside parties to consult with the federal government, nor does it create advisory bodies or public comment periods. The definition explicitly excludes applications for grants, and this text merely modifies the eligibility and funding amounts for such grants.
qwen_block.s: Section 41601(b) of the Violence Against Women Act of 1994 (42 U.S.C. 14043g(b)) is amended

opus.w: This section makes technical amendments to a grant program for sexual assault services. It changes who is eligible, how the Attorney General allocates money among States and territories, and how much funding is authorized. It mentions nongovernmental organizations and tribal programs, which could look like outside involvement, but they appear only as grant recipients. Nothing here requires consultation, hearings, comment periods, advisory bodies, or a right to sue before a federal decision.
opus.s: by inserting “or tribal programs and activities” after “nongovernmental organizations”

qwen_chat.w: This section amends the authorization and allocation formulas for grants to states and territories. The definition explicitly excludes 'applications for benefits or grants' from the scope of participation. There is no requirement for consultation, public comment, or advisory boards involving outside parties in the decision-making process described here.
qwen_chat.s: (a) Grants to States and Territories.—Section 41601(b) of the Violence Against Women Act of 1994 (42 U.S.C. 14043g(b)) is amended—
qwen_chat.b:
Temptation: It looks like participation because it mentions grants to states and territories, which are outside entities.
Resolution: The definition explicitly states that applications for benefits or grants are not participation. This section only amends the authorization and allocation formulas for grants, not the process of public consultation or decision-making involving outsiders.
